# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is for anyone who needs to produce a technical handbook that another person can trust, review and maintain. It is written for software, operations, architecture, security, data and other technical practitioners, and for the editors, reviewers and owners who support them. Readers need no local toolchain; the commands appear only for contributors who want to verify the repository.

The book is deliberately more about editorial decisions than about a particular publishing product. A tool can render Markdown, but it cannot decide who the reader is, what the handbook excludes, which evidence makes a claim acceptable or who may approve a release. Those decisions are the subject of Part I. Part II turns them into research, writing and review practice. Part III closes the lifecycle with reproducible release and maintenance.

Every chapter uses the same section shape: a reader outcome, the definitions and boundaries needed to make a decision, an illustrative example, a failure mode, a trade-off and a checklist where action is required. Examples with fictional names, targets or measurements are labeled illustrative. External sources are listed at the end of each chapter so a reader can check them rather than trusting the prose.

This is a draft manuscript, not a released edition. It has no publication manifest, checksums or catalog entry yet. The publication workflow is described in Chapter 7 as a platform process; that description is not evidence that this book has completed a release.

Use the book as a whole or follow one of the reading paths that follow. If a chapter is used as a team reference, keep the example and the checklist with the chapter: the vocabulary without the decision is easy to quote and easy to misuse.
